usageNotes: Use this to audit the APT repository configuration on a specific node — useful before running updates, after a PVE version upgrade, or when troubleshooting package availability. Requires Sys.Audit on /nodes/{node}; the node must be online and reachable by the API. Check the 'errors' array in the response first — parse failures on malformed .list or .sources files will appear there and may silently block package operations.

examples.summary: Fetch APT repository info for node pve1

tips: The 'digest' field in the top-level response covers all parsed files; use it as an optimistic-concurrency token when pairing with a write operation that modifies repositories.

The 'standard-repos' array lists well-known Proxmox repositories (e.g., pve-no-subscription, enterprise) and shows whether each is enabled — a quick way to confirm subscription vs. community repo state.
Repositories with 'Enabled: false' are still parsed and returned; check the 'Enabled' field on each entry rather than assuming all returned repos are active.
The 'infos' array surfaces warnings (e.g., deprecated suite names or redundant entries) that do not prevent parsing but may cause unexpected behavior during upgrades.
